The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations stating, inter alia, that the plaintiff's suit has no case of action, the suit is not maintainable and it is hit by limitation and Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and defendant Nos.1 and 2 as heirs of their father Rosmoy datta, were the owners in possession of the suit land; the brother in law of the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 103 of 1996 for declaration that the document is void and the plaintiff mutated her name in the record of the suit land illegally and secretly and when defendants submitted objection, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 17 of 1996 and although Rosmoy Datta died in the year 1985, the plaintiff could not get anything with the help of the said muktipatra during his life time and the record in the suit land was prepared in the name of owner Rosmoy Datta, who took jote settlement of the suit land from its original owner by way of a patta; Shailendra Das and plaintiff's story of settlement was forged and the defendants are in possession of the rest land and defendants filed Title Suit No.103 of 1996 for recovery of possession of the suit land; the plaintiff created some papers in favour of Hasan Khatun and inducted her into possession on .0550 decimals of land within the suit land including a total land of .06 18 decimals which was under the possession of the plaintiff by force and for recovery of the same the said suit was filed and the plaintiff's suit has been filed with false statement which is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. It appears from the record that the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.17 of 1996 for permanent injunction which was decreed in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner but on appeal the decision of the trial Court was reversed by the Court of Appeal below. The respondent instituted Title Suit No.103 of 1996 for declaration that the registered nadabinama dated 16.10.79 executed and registered by Rosmoy Dutta, predecessor, in favour of defendant No.1, regarding the suit land is illegal, forged and not binding on the respondent and also for recovery of khas possession of the suit land. It appears that an Advocate commissioner held a local inspection and submitted report before the Court being exhibited 10 and 10A wherein it was stated that the land in dispute is not the same land in dispute, although the plaintiff in Title Suit No.178 of 1996 i.e. the present  petitioner clearly stated that she has homestead in the land in dispute, which is in contradictory to the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner. It is the specific finding of the Court of appeal below that the petitioner could not prove by submitting documentary evidence that she has possession on the suit land for which the Court of appeal below found that the petitioner is not entitled to get a decree for permanent injunction. On the other hand, the Court of appeal below also found that the land which was the subject matter of the muktipatra and claimed by petitioner as the land in dispute is not the same land because the plaintiff of Title Suit No.17 of 1996 i.e. the present petitioner failed to prove that they obtained settlement from the Zamindar by submitting dakhilas for which the said nadabipatra is not binding upon the them. The Court of appeal below found that from the perusal of the cheque/dakhilas, exhibit-2 series and the certified copy of the patta, exhibit-'Kha', that although in the cheque/dakhilas the name of the pattadar was found but the identification of the suit land and the patta number were not mentioned in it correctly. The certified copy of the patta, exhibit kha, as produced by the opposite party, shows that the land is number patta within the land of old 201/1 to 209/2 it could not be ascertained as to whether the dakhilas exhibited before the Court were related to the disputed land or not. The Court of appeal below also found that the same person   put the signatures of Shailendra Kumar and Nagendra Kumar in the dakhilas and the petitioner did not take any step to get the signatures proved for which the Court of appeal below found that the cheque/dakhilas of the settlement which were exhibited by way of exhibit 2 series are forged and concocted and were prepared in order to prove title in the name of the Zaminder inasmuch as in the cheque dakhilas there is no reference of patta number.
